properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA family shipped via hash.js in the Ethereum signing stack (elliptic uses it internally); low quantum urgency (Grover only). Transitive dependency — no direct first-party call site needed for it to be part of what the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 implementation shipped in the dependency tree via crypto-js; collision-broken, but no direct first-party MD5 call site found — recorded as part of what the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 implementation shipped via crypto-js in the dependency tree; collision-broken hash, no direct first-party call site seen.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (at least Node.js 1.0.1)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: On-chain secp256k1 ECDSA is fixed by the Ethereum protocol (ecrecover precompile): changeable only at the chain level, not in this repo. What this repo controls is that it ships and invokes ECDSA verification in its Links/LinksNFT contracts through the gasless meta-transaction flow. The live recover call sites are Links.sol:90/169 and LinksNFT.sol:78/145 (ECDSA.recover on the OZ library), filed separately as findings for the GnosisSafe contract, which uses the precompile directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH surface shipped via elliptic, the EC library the Ethereum stack (eth-crypto/eccrypto) uses for ECIES key agreement on secp256k1; quantum-vulnerable key establishment — retroactive risk wherever it protects captured traffic.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 (crypto_box key agreement) shipped via tweetnacl; quantum-vulnerable key agreement present in the shipped tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: devDependency in the contract/keystore tooling chain; scrypt is the memory-hard password KDF used for Ethereum keystore/mnemonic secret derivation in the wallet toolchain. Changeable here by swapping the package or its parameters.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: XSalsa20-Poly1305 (crypto_secretbox) shipped via tweetnacl in the dependency tree — strong classical AE but a stream cipher + MAC, not PQ; recorded as part of what the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-only PKI: self-signed X.509 certificate generation for the local webpack-dev-server HTTPS endpoint; not a production trust anchor, but it is the certificate-lifecycle asset this repo ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge is the X.509/PKI/RSA toolkit backing the dev-server's self-signed cert generation; RSA keygen surface also present in the shipped tree (see the separate RSA yarn.lock object held by the other shard).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The manifest line is real and stays in the dependency inventory, but note the attribution error: npm's `crypto` package is a deprecated empty placeholder, not Node's OpenSSL binding. Under Node's module resolution, core modules win over node_modules, so any require('crypto') in this project resolves to the built-in OpenSSL-backed module — the OpenSSL algorithms this project can reach come from the runtime, not from this declared package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js ships MD5/SHA-1/SHA-2/AES implementations; transitive dependency with no direct first-party import found so far — still part of what the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the secp256k1 EC library at the heart of the Ethereum signing stack (eth-crypto, eccrypto, ethereumjs-util all sit on it) — its ECDH/ECDSA surface ships with this build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: One logical asset, two views: this LIB object records the declared dependency named `crypto`; ALG-ef098888 records the same package.json line with an OpenSSL attribution. The declaration is real; the npm `crypto@1.0.1` package itself is an empty placeholder, so actual OpenSSL reach comes from Node's built-in module at runtime.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 is the password KDF used by the Ethereum keystore (V3 wallet) decryption path in the web3 stack; iteration-count posture is decided by whichever caller invokes it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge also ships RSA keygen/sign and a TLS implementation alongside X.509 — the full toolkit is in the shipped tree for the dev HTTPS cert path.
